title: Pre-Analysis — Corrosion-Resistant Cabin Floor Seat Track for the Wet Zones
abstract: Pre-analysis of the corrosion-resistant seat track standard for the galley and lavatory zones, covering the cabin conversion work that has already replaced part of the run, the repairs in the field and the floor wiring the change disturbs.

sections.objective: Establish how much of the target population has already had part of its wet zone track replaced by earlier cabin work, whether an aircraft carrying a published splice repair can be modified at all, and what the two millimetre track height change does to the monument attachment interface and to the systems immediately under the floor.
sections.scope_note: The search covers ATA 53-50 as the primary chapter, 25-20 because the galley and lavatory monuments attach to the run, 38-30 because the aft lavatory drain path shares the same floor bay, and 92-31 because the aft floor carries a wiring run. ATA 33 cabin lighting was searched and excluded: the ceiling is not disturbed. The population was restricted to the lessor's redelivery fleet, which is where every recorded finding sits.
sections.method_note: Entity linking was seeded from the five part numbers, the single FIN, the drawing and the three zones on the candidate. Semantic similarity used two seed phrases about corrosion at a fitting slot under a galley and about a floor structure change that a cabin refresh can absorb. The strongest result of the round came from similarity rather than from entity linking: the rear cabin conversion work reads as a cabin programme and shares no identifier with a floor structure change, yet it has already replaced part of the same run on an unknown number of aircraft.
sections.findings_summary: Six items are confirmed and two of them block. The first blocker is the rear cabin conversion: on aircraft that have had it, part of the aft run has already been replaced to a different section, and the candidate would either duplicate that work or splice two different sections together, which is not substantiated. Nobody in the structures office knew this, because the conversion is recorded as a cabin change and shares no part number with the floor structure. The second blocker is the published splice repair, which the redelivery fleet carries at a rate of nineteen metres per aircraft; there is no substantiation for the new section spliced to a repaired run and the repair cannot simply be left in place. The floor wiring finding is an entity hit on a bus bar that nobody expected to see in a structures search, and it is real: the support is attached to the track that is being replaced. The remaining findings are consequential publication changes.
sections.next_steps: Establish, with the cabin programme, which aircraft in the target population have had the rear cabin conversion and what section their aft run now carries; this governs the whole applicability statement. Obtain a repair design position on modifying a run that carries a splice, including whether the splice can be removed. Commission a re-support scheme for the aft floor wiring at the affected stations. Confirm the monument attachment interface against the two millimetre height change.

similarity_seeds: corrosion at a seat track fitting slot under a galley or lavatory
floor structure change absorbed inside a cabin refresh rather than a structural visit

tasks.title: Identify aircraft that have had the rear cabin conversion
Obtain a repair design position on modifying a spliced run
Assess the aft floor wiring support at the affected stations
Check the monument attachment interface against the height change

evidence.similarity_note: The bulletin is written as a rear cabin conversion and talks about galley complexes and stowage; the candidate is written as a floor structure change and talks about extrusions and fitting slots. They share no part number and no zone, and the overlap was only visible once the conversion's own work scope was read.

expected_findings.rationale: On aircraft that have had the rear cabin conversion, part of the aft run has already been replaced to a different section. The candidate would either repeat that work or splice two different sections together, and neither case is substantiated.
expected_findings.resolution: Obtain the conversion embodiment list and exclude the already converted bays from the candidate applicability.

evidence.similarity_note: Both texts are about the aft cabin and about hard points that carry a monument, but one is written in cabin engineering language about galley complexes and deep stowage and the other in structures language about extrusions and drained channels. No identifier is shared.

expected_findings.rationale: The cabin-flex rear galley arrangement moves the monument hard points that the candidate's new track has to carry. The two changes have been developed in different offices and neither references the other.
expected_findings.resolution: Coordinate the hard point positions with the cabin programme before the track section is frozen.

expected_findings.rationale: The bus bar at the aft lavatory station is supported off the track that the candidate replaces. The wiring sheet requires a disturbed support to be re-established rather than re-clipped, which is design work and cannot be written as a cabin task.
expected_findings.resolution: Commission a re-support scheme for the affected stations before the modification is launched.

expected_findings.rationale: The redelivery fleet carries the bolted doubler and the splice repair at an average of nineteen metres per aircraft. No substantiation exists for the new section spliced to a repaired run, and the repair cannot simply be left in place under a new track.
expected_findings.resolution: Obtain a repair design position on whether a repaired run can be modified and add a pre-embodiment survey to the work package.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure carries the track sections in fixed lengths with quantities that depend on the cabin layout. A second section with a different height needs its own sheet and an effectivity note.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a publication change request once the section is frozen.

expected_findings.rationale: The splice repair task limits the number of splices a run may carry and sets the seat fitting lock check. Both change with the new section and the limit has to be restated for a mixed run.
expected_findings.resolution: Re-issue the repair task with the new section and a statement on mixed runs.

expected_non_findings.reason: Same floor structure sub-chapter and almost identical corrosion vocabulary, but it repairs cargo floor panels below the cabin floor. It shares no seat track, no fitting slot and no monument hard point with the candidate.

Returned by the shared cabin and cargo lining vocabulary and by the removal of floor panels, but it removes cargo compartment lining panels one deck below and has no interface with the cabin floor seat track run.

type_data.conclusion: Not yet issued. Two blocking items: the rear cabin conversion overlap, which was invisible to entity linking, and the population of runs already carrying a splice repair.
